html:
The territory of the Roman Republic as the map shows it in 323 and 200 BCE: first central Italy, then all of Italy with Sicily, Sardinia and the east and south of Spain.

In 323 BCE, the year Alexander died, Rome led a league of Latin and Italian allies and was fighting the Samnite Wars for central Italy. Victory there, and over King Pyrrhus of Epirus in the Pyrrhic War, gave it the peninsula south of the Po by about 270 BCE. Conquered peoples became allies who sent soldiers, not tribute, which gave Rome huge reserves of men.

That manpower decided the wars with Carthage. The First Punic War won Sicily in 241 BCE. In the Second Punic War Hannibal crossed the Alps and destroyed a Roman army at Cannae, yet Rome recovered, won at Zama in 202 BCE and took Spain. By 200 BCE it was turning east, toward Macedon and the Battle of Cynoscephalae. The state's full story is under Roman Republic.
sum: The territory of the Roman Republic as the map shows it in 323 and 200 BCE: first central Italy, then all of Italy with Sicily, Sardinia and the east and south of Spain.
